decisions.reason: As a bread product close to the core assortment, it likely required limited new investment but fits the firm's traditional identity, so management would tend to retain it unless range simplification becomes necessary.

The sweet pastry is also close to the established offer and easy to justify within the firm's heritage-based line, making continued commitment more likely than withdrawal despite only modest visible commitment.

This farmhouse bread is central to the bakery business and can be defended as a natural extension of the craft range, though as a newer and fairly substitutable loaf it is somewhat more droppable than older core items.
The poppy seed Christmas stollen received a gold award and was given its own page, creating public commitment and a strong basis for management to continue backing it as a festive flagship product.
The premium Christmas stollen also carries a gold award and matches the firm's seasonal specialty positioning, so management has clear reputational reasons to keep it on the market.
